gaps.sentence: All new students ___ (give) a locker key on their first day.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: are + given. Passives of give keep the indirect object as subject.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript might ___ if you keep touching it with bare hands.
gaps.explanation: Get + past participle (get damaged) is an informal passive common with mishaps.

gaps.sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.

gaps.sentence: This machine ___ (NOT USE) for years before I repaired it.
gaps.hint: negative passive before a past point
gaps.explanation: The disuse continued up to the past repair: past perfect passive hadn't been used.

gaps.sentence: The house looked deserted; it ___ (empty) years earlier.
gaps.hint: past event before another past point
gaps.explanation: 'Years earlier' is before the past reference point, so past perfect passive: had been + emptied.

gaps.sentence: Passengers ___ (ask) to fasten their seatbelts before take-off.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: are + asked. The agent (crew) is obvious and omitted.

gaps.sentence: The bridge ___ by a locally trained architect.
gaps.explanation: 'Was designed by' — passive with the agent in a by-phrase.

gaps.sentence: The archives ___ (CAN SEE) by appointment only.
gaps.explanation: Modal + be + participle: can be seen.
